selected_graph_nodes.original_theorem:
ASTIS-authored sufficient noncompact C2 Gaussian background independently sealed before proof.
For every finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert/Borel space E, including rank zero, let gamma be literal stdGaussian E. Every signed real globally C2 f with actual f in L2(gamma), true gradient f in L2(gamma), and Phi(f²) integrable satisfies homogeneous Ent_gamma(f²)<=2 integral norm(gradient f)^2. The actual cutoff mass, entropy and gradient-energy limits are proved internally. Phi(t)=t log t is continuous at zero; neither positive mass nor normalization nor compact support is assumed.
Exact scope: Actual stdGaussian E on finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel E, signed globally C2 f with real fL2/gradientL2/Phi(f²)L1 domains. These are produced by actual32 for its true sqrt-density. No cutoff limit/desired inequality/domain-of-repaired-density/law/energy certificate premises. Genuine noncompact function-LSI coefficient2 through internally derived actual cutoff limits; rank0/zero mass retained. Coherent33 KL/Fisher, full weak W12 extension, separate GaussianT2/FIRST4.6/both paper main/error/cost/composition/fullreader remain OPEN.
theorem gaussian_logSobolev_of_contDiff
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f)
    (hf2 : MemLp f 2 (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E))
    (hgrad2 : MemLp (gradient f) 2 (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E))
    (hentropy : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2))
      (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)) :
    let γ : Measure E := ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E
    (∫ x, (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2) ∂γ) -
      (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂γ) * Real.log (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂γ) ≤
      2 * ∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂γ

selected_graph_nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space E equipped with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure, including dimension zero, let gamma be the canonical centered Gaussian measure with variance one in each orthonormal coordinate. For every signed real-valued function f on E which is globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable, assume f and its literal global gradient are genuinely in L2(gamma), and assume x -> f(x)^2 log(f(x)^2) is integrable with respect to gamma. Then
integral f(x)^2 log(f(x)^2) dgamma - (integral f(x)^2 dgamma) log(integral f(x)^2 dgamma) <= 2 integral ||gradient f(x)||^2 dgamma.
The gradient is the Riesz representation of the real Frechet derivative and the norm is the Hilbert norm. All integrals are real Bochner integrals; log is totalized at zero and the product t log t is interpreted continuously at t=0. The assertion requires no positivity of f or of its square mass, and no normalization, compact support, additional cutoff limit, or inequality certificate.
